findings.claim: The objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; coordinate contrasts are therefore proxies, not the affinity objective itself.

The learning/control support is the score-clock window [0.0, 0.5] with 50 observed score nodes at 0.01 spacing; curve support is [0.0, 0.49], so no extrapolation beyond the observed nodes is licensed.

Across the 20 landmark soft-mass features, whole-window z magnitudes are small (largest |z| ~0.64 for landmark_00_soft_mass) while first/last rate z values are large and of opposite sign (e.g. landmark_00 first_rate_z ~ +9.3, last_rate_z ~ -10.0; landmark_10 first_rate_z ~ +66.3, last_rate_z ~ -11.6; landmark_11 first_rate_z ~ -66.3, last_rate_z ~ +10.8). This indicates changing local contrast/rate rather than a stationary whole-window level shift.

No polynomial trend is accepted for any inspected soft-mass feature (polynomial_accepted=false, relative_node_RMSE ~0.29-0.70) and sign_changes range 4-8 with strong_sign_conflicts up to 11, so a single smooth monotone stage profile is not supported by these rows.
Stage profiles and temporal profiles are reported unavailable, so no data-derived knot or stage boundary can be claimed from profiles; only the continuous curves and trend rows are available.

hypotheses.direction: rate contrast changes sign from positive early to negative late; whole-window level near zero
hypotheses.falsifier: A re-read of the landmark_00_soft_mass curve showing no sign change in local rate, or a whole-window z comparable in magnitude to the rate z values.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass continuous curve over score nodes [0.0, 0.49]
hypotheses.scope: global over observed score nodes; landmark_00 region
hypotheses.statement: Landmark_00 soft-mass shows a signed early-positive to late-negative rate contrast over the observed score window, consistent with a time-dependent (not stationary) coordinate contrast at that landmark.

hypotheses.direction: opposite-sign early vs late rates at both landmarks
hypotheses.falsifier: Curve reads showing first and last rate z of the same sign, or whole-window z dominating the rate z values.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_10_soft_mass and landmark_11_soft_mass continuous curves over score nodes [0.0, 0.49]
hypotheses.scope: global over observed score nodes; landmark_10 and landmark_11 regions
hypotheses.statement: Landmark_10 and landmark_11 soft-mass show large opposite-sign first/last rate z values, indicating a changing contrast that a constant-blend teacher would not reproduce.

hypotheses.direction: gradual change in teacher relevance rather than a sharp knot
hypotheses.falsifier: A reproducible knot supported by independently stable profiles, or evidence that a constant blend reproduces the observed contrast equally well.
hypotheses.observable: soft-mass contrast curves across the full observed window
hypotheses.statement: Because no polynomial is accepted and sign changes are frequent, a gradual stage-dependent teacher relevance (as in the registered S1 observed-to-static recipe) is a testable hypothesis rather than a discovered stage boundary; a constant blend (S2) is the appropriate control.

limitations: Stage profiles and temporal profiles are unavailable; no data-derived stage boundary or knot can be asserted.
Trend rows are summaries; the underlying continuous curves were not individually read for every landmark, so per-landmark claims are limited to the cited rows.
Coordinate contrasts are proxies only; they do not establish affinity improvement, descendant survival, or any neural-module causation.
Selection preference and survival are not evidence of measured final benefit; no decoded final affinity labels were available in this input.
